title: Privacy, worth doing soon: reminders keep arriving that the screen says are off; the email's unsubscribe link is the person's only way out
evidence: Residual of H18e (US-17 AC17 Limit). Device A taps Turn off on active T1 while device B turns reminders on (Drive: A's cancel deletes the row, B inserts T2 and writes active T2). If A has not merged B's write before its own (the usual case: the 60 s poll, widget-src/src/lib/record-session.ts:38-39), A's cancelled T1 carries the later stamp and wins the opt-in merge (pickNewerOptional, time first then lamport, packages/health-core/src/merge.ts:423-427). End: the record says cancelled T1 on every device, the server row T2 stays live, pushes stop, and no Turn off in the app reaches T2. The fix is merge-level: a cancel beats an active opt-in only for its own token. A naive rule is not associative, so devices can diverge: aT2(t1), aT1(t3), cT1(t4) merge to cT1 one way and aT1 the other. Design note with a convergence proof first; merge semantics, health-core, engine release. Source: the H18e design note (Option C).
